members.name: vix_filtered_index_trend_v126
members.thesis: When VIX is low, index trends tend to be slow and steady. When VIX is high, trends are erratic but offer massive reward/risk. Filtering trend breakouts by VIX regime prevents trading noisy chop. Exists due to systemic risk pricing.
entry_long: india_vix > 14 AND CROSSOVER(ema_9, ema_21) AND close > VWAP(close)
entry_short: india_vix > 14 AND CROSSUNDER(ema_9, ema_21) AND close < VWAP(close)
weaknesses: VIX is forward-filled and can be lagged intraday
High VIX means wider stop losses are required, reducing position size
Whipsaw risk in contracting volatility environments

members.name: vix_regime_breakout_v1
members.thesis: When India VIX spikes sharply intraday (>10% increase from prior close), it signals fear-driven selling. Historically, these spikes are short-lived and mean-revert within hours. The inefficiency exists because retail traders panic-sell during VIX spikes, creating temporary dislocations in liquid nam
filters: vix spike > 10% from prior close (entry condition, not a filter)
no entry before 10:00 (let panic settle) or after 14:30
volume must be > 1.5x average (confirming real selling, not thin drift)
skip if spread > 0.15% (too illiquid during panic)
weaknesses: VIX spikes caused by genuine regime change (war, financial crisis) do NOT mean-revert intraday. The VIX 30 cap helps but isn't foolproof. 2020 March would have been a bloodbath.
Low frequency: signal fires maybe 2-4 times per month. Not enough trades for statistical significance in short backtests.
Slippage during VIX spikes is extreme — 5 bps may be optimistic. Real fills in panicky markets can be 10+ bps.
members.prior_art: VIX mean-reversion is well-known in options literature. Adapted to equity intraday context. See CBOE research papers.

members.name: vix_mean_reversion_intraday_v1
members.thesis: India VIX itself mean-reverts within the trading day. When VIX drops > 3% from its opening value by mid-morning, it tends to recover partially, and vice versa. This intraday VIX pattern creates a tradeable signal for Nifty50 stocks: when VIX drops sharply (complacency), go short high-beta stocks ant
entry_long: vix_change_from_open > 3 (VIX has spiked > 3% intraday — fear spike)
vix > vix_ema_30 (VIX above its intraday average — room to mean revert down)
filters: core to strategy — only trade when VIX moves > 3% from its open
no entries before 10:00 (let VIX stabilize) or after 14:30
target stocks must have normal volume
counter-trend by design — VIX spike = long; VIX drop = short
weaknesses: VIX spikes > 3% intraday are infrequent — maybe 5-8 times per month; low trade frequency
In genuine crisis (geopolitical, COVID), VIX spike is one-way and doesn't revert same day
High-beta stocks during VIX spikes have wider spreads, increasing slippage to 4+ bps
members.prior_art: VIX intraday mean reversion — documented in US market (CBOE VIX). India VIX adaptation.

members.name: vix_regime_switch_v1
members.thesis: India VIX mean-reverts after extreme readings. When VIX spikes above its 20-day Bollinger Band upper (> 2 SD), it signals peak fear, and Nifty50 stocks tend to bounce within 1-2 sessions. Conversely, when VIX drops below its lower band, complacency sets in and a correction follows. Intraday, you can
entry_long: vix > vix_bb_upper (VIX is elevated — fear regime)
vix_change_60 < 0 (VIX starting to decline from peak)
entry_short: vix < vix_bb_lower (VIX is depressed — complacency regime)
vix_change_60 > 0 (VIX starting to rise from trough)
members.exit_target: 0.6% from entry (larger target because of multi-hour hold)
filters: core to strategy — trade only when VIX is at extremes
no entries first 30 min (let VIX stabilize) or last 30 min
skip if spread > 0.1% (wider during high VIX)
weaknesses: Very low frequency — VIX extremes happen maybe 2-3 times per month; long idle periods
During genuine crises (COVID, geopolitical), VIX can stay elevated for weeks — mean reversion is delayed
High-beta stocks during VIX spikes have wide spreads and volatile fills — slippage is 4+ bps
members.prior_art: VIX mean reversion — well-documented in US markets (VXX trading). India VIX version is less studied.

members.name: vix_mean_reversion_v1
members.universe: NIFTYBEES or top-5 NIFTY 50 constituents by weight on NSE
members.thesis: India VIX exhibits strong intraday mean-reversion after spikes. When VIX jumps >8% within 30 minutes (typically on sudden NIFTY selloffs), it reverts at least 50% of the spike within 2 hours roughly 70% of the time. This is because VIX spikes are driven by panic option buying (puts), which creates a
entry_short: VIX_30min_change < -6 (VIX crushed >6% in 30 mins — complacency spike)
members.exit_target: VIX reverts 50% of spike (VIX_30min_change halves) OR NIFTY recovers 50% of drawdown
members.exit_stop: VIX makes new session high (spike continuing) OR NIFTY drops another 0.5% from entry
filters: core signal — requires VIX spike >8% in 30 mins
VIX spikes after 14:00 IST less likely to revert within session; prefer morning spikes
NIFTY option volume must be elevated (confirming VIX spike is real, not stale data)
NIFTY must not have broken a major support level (200-SMA on daily) — structural breaks don't revert
bid-ask on entry vehicle < 0.08% (spreads widen during VIX spikes)
weaknesses: The strategy buys the dip during fear spikes — during genuine crises (2020 COVID, 2022 Russia-Ukraine), VIX spikes DON'T revert and the strategy takes large losses on consecutive signals
VIX spike frequency is low (8%+ spikes in 30 min happen ~3-5 times per month), making this capital-inefficient as a standalone strategy
Wider bid-ask spreads during VIX spikes increase effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, significantly cutting into the edge
members.prior_art: Whaley (2000) VIX as fear gauge; Daigler & Rossi (2006) VIX mean reversion. Simon & Campasano (2014) VIX futures roll and mean reversion.

members.name: vix_regime_switch_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 20 by liquidity)
members.thesis: India VIX transitions between regimes (low <13, normal 13-18, elevated 18-25, crisis >25) and the optimal intraday strategy differs by regime. In low-VIX regimes, mean-reversion strategies dominate (tight ranges, reliable VWAP pulls). In elevated-VIX regimes, momentum and breakout strategies outperf
entry_long: IF vix_regime == 'low' OR 'normal': close < BB_lower AND RSI_14 < 30 AND ADX_14 < 25 (mean reversion mode)
IF vix_regime == 'elevated': close > EMA_9 AND EMA_9 > EMA_21 AND ADX_14 > 25 (momentum mode)
entry_short: IF vix_regime == 'low' OR 'normal': close > BB_upper AND RSI_14 > 70 AND ADX_14 < 25 (mean reversion mode)
IF vix_regime == 'elevated': close < EMA_9 AND EMA_9 < EMA_21 AND ADX_14 > 25 (momentum mode)
members.exit_target: mean_rev: SMA(close, 20) (midline reversion); momentum: 1.5 * ATR_14 from entry
members.exit_stop: mean_rev: 0.3 * ATR_14 beyond BB; momentum: 0.8 * ATR_14 from entry
filters: core of the strategy — VIX regime determines sub-strategy; crisis regime (VIX > 25) = no trading
mean_rev mode: ADX < 25 required; momentum mode: ADX > 25 required
weaknesses: VIX regime boundaries (13, 18, 25) are arbitrary and may not be optimal; the strategy is sensitive to these thresholds and may generate whipsaw signals near boundaries
Switching between mean-reversion and momentum sub-strategies mid-day (if VIX crosses a boundary) can cause confusion and partial signals from the prior regime
The combined strategy has more parameters (7+) than a single-regime strategy, increasing overfitting risk in backtesting
members.prior_art: Ang & Bekaert (2004) regime-switching models; Baele et al. (2019) VIX-based strategy timing. Indian VIX regime thresholds calibrated from Banerjee & Sarkar (2006) on India VIX behavior.

members.name: vix_bucket_strategy_v1
members.thesis: India VIX provides a forward-looking measure of expected market volatility derived from NIFTY option prices. By bucketing VIX into 4 regimes — Calm (VIX < 13), Normal (13-18), Elevated (18-24), and Crisis (> 24) — and assigning a different strategy to each bucket, we adapt to the macroeconomic uncer
entry_long: CALM: close < BB_lower_calm AND close < vwap AND RSI(close,10) < 30
NORMAL: EMA(close,9) crosses above EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
ELEVATED: close > Supertrend(10,4.0) AND close > vwap AND volume > 2*SMA(volume,20)
entry_short: CALM: close > BB_upper_calm AND close > vwap AND RSI(close,10) > 70
NORMAL: EMA(close,9) crosses below EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
ELEVATED: close < Supertrend(10,4.0) AND close < vwap AND volume > 2*SMA(volume,20)
members.exit_target: CALM: 20 bps; NORMAL: 35 bps; ELEVATED: 60 bps
members.exit_stop: CALM: 12 bps; NORMAL: 20 bps; ELEVATED: 35 bps
filters: VIX_Bucket itself is the primary filter — CRISIS bucket = no trading
No entries before 09:25 or after 15:10; CALM can trade until 15:15
ELEVATED: strict 2x volume required; CALM/NORMAL: SMA(volume,15) sufficient
NORMAL: NIFTY trend must agree; CALM/ELEVATED: no trend filter
CALM: spread < 3 bps; NORMAL: < 5 bps; ELEVATED: < 8 bps
weaknesses: VIX bucket boundaries (13, 18, 24) are arbitrary and may not represent true regime shifts — the optimal boundaries likely vary over multi-year cycles as structural volatility changes
India VIX can jump from 14 to 19 within minutes during a shock, causing an immediate regime switch and forced exit from current position at a loss
CRISIS bucket (VIX > 24) has historically offered some of the best mean-reversion opportunities, but the strategy avoids them entirely, missing high-conviction trades
members.prior_art: VIX-conditional strategies common in US equity options trading; Whaley (2009) on VIX; VIX-based strategy selection discussed in Sinclair's 'Volatility Trading'; India VIX-specific research limited

members.name: ma_crossover_momentum_v1
members.thesis: Exploiting short-term momentum from 9/21 EMA crossover with volume in trending sessions. Inefficiency from lag in retail response to cross. Survives due to index filter and VIX cap preventing whipsaws.
weaknesses: Regime dependency: choppy markets cause whipsaws
Slippage on fast moves during cross
Crowding: MA crossover taught everywhere on X
members.prior_art: MA Crossover (listed in StockX India X thread)

members.name: vix_spike_mean_reversion
members.thesis: Exploits 'Volatility Overpricing'. A sudden 5% spike in India VIX within 10 minutes often leads to an over-reaction in Nifty 50 component prices. As VIX stabilizes, the delta-hedging pressure from option writers subsides, leading to a quick price recovery. This is a market microstructure constraint.
weaknesses: VIX spikes can lead to sustained crashes (regime change)
Slippage is high during high VIX

members.name: momentum_exhaustion_vix_reversal
members.thesis: Exploits behavioral panic/euphoria. When VIX spikes intraday along with a vertical price move, retail traders capitulate. The resulting volume climax exhausts the move. Institutional 'dark pools' absorb the volume at extreme levels, leading to mean reversion.
weaknesses: Catching falling knives
High slippage on volume climaxes
